status: frozen before training any classifier (the zoo is being built)
question: Do exact weight-space programs give useful data augmentation for weight-space learning? Classifiers that read INR weights (NFN, NFT, graph metanetworks) are data-hungry and reach far lower accuracy on INR zoos than pixel classifiers on the images; existing weight-space augmentations are permutations and mixup, which do not change the represented image. Coordinate-layer and readout programs produce the weights of a genuinely transformed image (shift, flip, rotation, zoom, contrast, brightness) exactly, at any depth, for the cost of a matrix product.

data.train: zoo/mnist_s32_train5k: 5,000 SIRENs (2-32-32-1) on MNIST train images 0..4999, PyTorch trainer, 2,000 Adam steps, seed = 0 + chunk offset
data.test: zoo/mnist_s32_test1k: 1,000 SIRENs on MNIST test images 1000..1999 (disjoint from every earlier zoo, which used test 0..59)

augmentations.programs: random translation by (dy, dx) ~ U(-2, 2) pixels (continuous, exact on the function: c1 -= d A1), horizontal flip with p = 0.5 (A1[1,:] *= -1), rotation by U(-15, 15) degrees (A1 <- R A1), zoom U(0.9, 1.1) (A1 /= z), contrast U(0.8, 1.25) and brightness U(-0.1, 0.1) on the readout
augmentations.control_permute: random hidden-unit permutations and sign flips of both hidden layers (function-preserving; the standard weight-space augmentation)

classifiers.deepsets2: a two-level permutation-invariant network written for this study: layer-1 units are embedded from their (frequency vector, phase); layer-2 units from their bias, their readout weight and a DeepSets pooling over their incoming weights paired with the layer-1 unit embeddings; a final DeepSets pooling over layer-2 units. Invariant to both hidden permutations; sign-flip symmetry handled by canonicalising each unit's sign (largest incoming weight positive).
classifiers.aligned_mlp: weights aligned to one reference network with wsinr.align, flattened, 2-hidden-layer MLP (the naive baseline)
classifiers.training: AdamW, 60 epochs, lr 1e-3 with cosine decay, batch 64, cross-entropy, label = MNIST digit; test accuracy at the last epoch

predictions_frozen_before_running.G1_programs_help: With 1,000 training INRs, program augmentation raises deepsets2 test accuracy by at least 5 points over no augmentation (mean of 3 seeds).
predictions_frozen_before_running.G2_better_than_permutation: Program augmentation beats permutation/sign-flip augmentation by at least 3 points at 1,000 training INRs (permutations are exact symmetries of an invariant model and should add little).
predictions_frozen_before_running.G3_data_efficiency: deepsets2 with programs at 1,000 INRs matches or exceeds deepsets2 without augmentation at 2,000 INRs.
predictions_frozen_before_running.G4_also_for_the_naive_model: aligned_mlp gains at least 3 points from program augmentation at 1,000 INRs.
predictions_frozen_before_running.G5_gap_closes_with_data: The gain of programs over no augmentation at 5,000 INRs is smaller than at 500 (augmentation matters most in the small-data regime).

controls: pixel-space upper reference: a small CNN on the rendered images of the same INRs, with and without the same image-space augmentations, to show what the augmentation is worth when applied to pixels
augmentation applied on the fly per batch, fresh parameters each epoch
test INRs never augmented; test images disjoint from all earlier zoos
decision_rule: If G1-G3 hold, weight-space augmentation is the paper's application pillar and is extended to Fashion-MNIST and to a CIFAR colour zoo on GPU. If G1 fails, the permutation-invariant model is already saturated on this zoo and the experiment moves to the harder CIFAR zoo before any conclusion.
